The provided abstract describes a comprehensive **review paper** on nanofluid Minimum Quantity Lubrication (MQL) in machining (turning, milling, and grinding), covering nanofluid preparation and properties, supply equipment and atomization mechanisms, flow field and wetting behavior, and future development roadmaps. The specific quantitative examples mentioned in the abstract involve jatropha oil-based alumina nanofluids (85% friction reduction vs. dry conditions), alumina nanoparticle cutting fluids in hard milling (177–230% tool life improvement), and carbon nanotube nanoparticles in normal saline (145.06% increase in convective heat transfer coefficient).

None of the four candidate hypotheses are supported by this evidence:
- **Hypothesis 1** proposes magnetorheological (MR) fluids with electrostatic atomization at 100 mT and 10–20 µm droplets (35% tool wear reduction, 20% Ra improvement), none of which appear in the abstract.
- **Hypothesis 2** proposes controlled comparative experiments with MoO3-based nanofluids, SDS, and polyethoxylated nonylphenol surfactants (0.45 vol%, 3:2 ratio, ≥30% improvement), none of which appear in the abstract.
- **Hypothesis 3** proposes 0.1 vol% Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles under a 0.5 T, 1 Hz magnetic field (40% tool life improvement, 25% energy reduction), none of which appear in the abstract.
- **Hypothesis 4** proposes an orthogonal turning experiment on AISI 1045 steel using mineral oil with 1 wt% 50 nm CuO nanoparticles under specific nozzle and cutting parameters (≥15% flank wear reduction, ≥20% Ra improvement), none of which appear in the abstract.

CHOICE: NONE
